title: How to Use SUMIF in Google Sheets
dek: SUMIF adds up numbers that meet a condition. The syntax is =SUMIF(range, criterion, sum_range) — for example, total sales for one region. Here is exactly how each part works, with examples.

sources.label: Google Docs Editors Help — SUMIF function

richText: SUMIF adds up only the numbers that meet a condition you set — like totaling the sales for one region, or adding only the expenses over a certain amount. It is one of the most useful functions in Google Sheets once your data grows past a simple list.

body.caption: The three parts of SUMIF
rows: The cells to test against your condition
The condition to match, like "North" or ">100"
The cells to add up (optional — if left out, SUMIF adds the range itself)

richText: Say column A has regions and column B has sales. To total the sales for the North region:
This checks A2:A100 for "North" and adds the matching values from B2:B100. Wrap text criteria in quotation marks. You can also test numbers — =SUMIF(B2:B100, ">100") adds every value over 100.

body.richText: Point the criterion at a cell instead of typing it: =SUMIF(A2:A100, D1, B2:B100) totals whatever region you type in D1, so one formula becomes a mini dashboard.

items.question: What is the difference between SUMIF and SUMIFS?
items.answerRichText: SUMIF adds values that meet one condition, with the sum range last. SUMIFS handles several conditions at once and puts the sum range first. Use SUMIF for a single test and SUMIFS when two or more must all be true.

items.question: How do I use SUMIF with a greater-than condition?
items.answerRichText: Put the operator and number in quotation marks as the criterion, like =SUMIF(B2:B100, ">100"). You can do the same with <, >=, and <= — for example ">=50" adds every value of 50 or more.

items.question: Why is my SUMIF returning 0?
items.answerRichText: Usually the criterion does not match — a trailing space, different text, or numbers stored as text. Check that the range and criterion line up, and that "North" in the data exactly matches the "North" in your formula.
